name: Panchhi Petha
why_it_matters: Founded 1926 by Pancham Lal Goyal — the brand most travellers associate with Agra petha. Multiple branches and many lookalike 'Panchhi'-named imitators in the city; the Hing ki Mandi flagship is the verifiable original counter.
insider_tip: The 'Panchhi Petha Store' on the official site lists exact authorised counters — rickshaw drivers will steer you to non-original shops with similar names for commission. Insist on Hing ki Mandi or Civil Lines branches.
signature_address: Hing Ki Mandi Road, near Agra Fort, Agra 282003

name: Deviram Sweets
signature_dish: bedai with aloo sabzi and jalebi
why_it_matters: Belanganj's 73-year-old breakfast counter — the city's reference plate for bedai (kachori made of urad dal) with spicy aloo sabzi, finished with hot jalebi to cut the heat. What chole bhature is to Delhi, this set is to Agra.
insider_tip: Bedai is served only 9am-2pm — the post-2pm jalebi is freshly fried but the bedai stops. Cash only; no seating, eat standing at the counter.

name: Rawatpara Bedai Stalls
why_it_matters: Rawatpara's Phulatti Bazaar lane is wall-to-wall bedai counters — same urad-dal kachori plus aloo-sabzi format as Deviram, in the older bazaar setting. Local food guides slot it as one of the top-10 city bedai zones.
insider_tip: No standout single shop here — pick the busiest counter. Open 7-11am only; eat fast and walk to Agra Fort entrance which is 1.2km north.
signature_address: Phulatti Bazaar, Rawatpara, Bodhi Ka Nagala, Mantola, Agra 282001
